passage_text: BACKGROUND AND SIGNIFICANCE: Obesity is common among persons with severe mental illness (SMI), especially those with bipolar disorder (BP) (1-5). It is estimated that 45-55% of people with SMI are obese, making obesity 1.5-2 times more common among those with SMI than among the general population. Indeed, in a recent pragmatic lithium trial conducted in BP, 69% of the subjects were overweight or obese. Although the precise mechanism underlying the relationship between obesity and SMI is unknown, it is thought to be multifactorial, involving genetic factors, intrinsic features of SMI (e.g., overeating, poor dietary choices, sedentary lifestyle, and sleep dysregulation), and the weight-gaining effects of most of the psychotropic medication used to treat SMI. Importantly, obesity is thought to contribute to the well-documented elevated mortality from cardiovascular disease (CVD) among those with BP. Thus, weight reduction in obese people with BP might be important for reducing their morbidity and mortality from CVD and other obesity-related conditions (e.g., diabetes and metabolic syndrome).
